Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2) displays a distinct opacity in the right lower lung field, indicated by the arrow. In the context of oncology imaging questions involving this specific finding, a solitary pulmonary nodule or mass is frequently presented as evidence of metastatic disease from an extrathoracic primary, such as breast carcinoma. Options suggesting the tumor is solely in the breast are incorrect as the pathology is clearly intrathoracic/pulmonary on this modality.
